title: Deck and document builder
summary: Plans a deck, a presentation or a branded document with you, then writes the source that Toilet Paper compiles. A deck source becomes an editable .pptx on the company master and one HTML file with the same look; a Markdown source becomes a Word document. It also starts an app page. It asks the format, the brand and the classification first, and writes nothing before you approve the plan.
use_when: You need a presentation, a report, a memo or an internal tool page that must look like the company.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test.

title: Report builder
summary: The delivery line for a Power BI report. The idea is a mockup first: the mockup writes the specification and the contract, and a set of gates checks the delivery. What runs today is the audit of the semantic model against a curation checklist (an automated pass, an assisted review, a score per category), and a record of the steps, gates and cost of a delivery.
use_when: You want to deliver a Power BI report, or to check a semantic model before it goes into one.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test. The audit is in beta.
ships: scripts (audit, report writer, step record, session cost)
wip: The mockup first, the specification and contract it writes, and the delivery gates are in design.
The mode that scaffolds a new report from a specification is in development.

title: Design review
summary: Reviews an HTML page against a design system while the page runs in a browser, at 3 screen widths, with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility checks and a measurement of the brand tokens.
use_when: You generate a dashboard, catalog, one-pager or web deck and want to know whether it follows the brand before you deliver it.

title: Project coach
summary: A pocket guide for running projects, anchored in a five-phase project process and the principles of PMBOK 7, pragmatic and not bureaucratic. It prepares a person for the conversation with a human mentor and does not replace it.
use_when: You ask how to start a project, what document you need, how to run a kick-off, a status report, a RACI or a closure, or how to handle risk, change, scope and stakeholders.
basis: Published to the team folder for a controlled test.

title: OKR cycle
summary: Runs a whole OKR cycle for a team: drafts and pressure-tests the OKRs, groups them into pillars, assigns owners, balances workload, defines a 75, 100 and 125 achievement-scoring model with weights, and generates executive one-pagers (bilingual HTML to PDF) and an Excel scorecard from a single spec file.
use_when: You plan or review OKRs, want to score achievement from 50 to 150 percent, or split objectives across people.

title: Fabric app method
summary: A method to create, develop and publish an app on Microsoft Fabric Apps with its CLI, in TypeScript: prepare the machine once, create the project with the team's rules, develop with an AI assistant, connect it to the data, review and publish.
use_when: You start a pilot app on Fabric, connect an app to a semantic model or publish one.

title: Product coach
summary: A pocket guide for defining what to build, the counterpart of the project coach. It writes a feature spec from a problem, updates a Now, Next, Later roadmap, turns research and feedback into themes and opportunities, and runs brainstorming that diverges and then converges.
use_when: You need a feature spec, a roadmap reprioritised, user feedback synthesised or ideas to solve a problem.
